implement.approach: Test-first: commit 476c57f7 adds a bounded child-process probe (existing 5000 ms / SIGKILL / --max-old-space-size=192 / 1 MiB maxBuffer harness, unchanged) asserting that requiring apps/mobile/metro.config.js leaves metro-transform-worker, metro-minify-terser and @babel/core unloaded while the ICNS decoder guard still rejects disguised bytes, and that the wrapper then hands a worker the identical upstream `transform`/`getCacheKey` functions; commit 997019d0 narrows the forbidden-module filter to modules only the eager worker require pulls in (Sentry's Metro serializer legitimately loads @babel/parser, @babel/generator and metro-transform-plugins during config). Fix commit f010c464 changes only apps/mobile/scripts/metro-asset-transformer.cjs: the image-size decoder guard still runs eagerly on module load (config process AND every fresh worker), but `module.exports` becomes `{ get transform(), get getCacheKey() }` getters that `require('metro-transform-worker')` on first access instead of at config time. Metro's Worker.flow.js and getTransformCacheKey.js `require.call(null, transformerPath)` and then read `.transform` / `.getCacheKey`, so the interface Metro (and Sentry's separate Babel pipeline) sees is unchanged. Existing suites drive a real `metro/private/DeltaBundler/Worker.transform` through config.transformerPath and pass, confirming the worker path. No timeout/memory/output guard changed; no prewarming, no test reordering, no retries.
regression_tests_added: apps/mobile/__tests__/wf/be-mobile-security-secrets.test.ts :: GUARD build dependency security > guards the config process without loading the transform-worker toolchain, then hands workers the upstream interface
residual_risks: The historical 5 s miss was reproduced only by artificially starving CPU (systemd CPUQuota=8%) through the real Jest harness; it did not occur in ordinary cold runs on this 16-vCPU box. Under sufficiently severe starvation (<=8% of one core here) the candidate still misses the deadline during process teardown after completing all work, so the fix removes the largest avoidable cost (~1.4 s under starvation) rather than making the 5 s / 192 MB guard immune to arbitrary CPU contention — which the package forbids addressing by raising the timeout.

metro-transform-worker is now required on first `transform`/`getCacheKey` access inside Metro workers rather than at config time; Metro 0.87.0 (Worker.flow.js, getTransformCacheKey.js) reads these as plain properties so getters are transparent. Any third-party tooling that enumerates or spreads the transformer module's own properties (none found in the repo, Sentry's metro plugin wraps `serializer`, not `transformerPath`) would need the getters evaluated.

implement.summary: DEFECT ON BASE_SHA (f250acd7): apps/mobile/scripts/metro-asset-transformer.cjs:16 `module.exports = require('metro-transform-worker')` executes eagerly when apps/mobile/metro.config.js:4 (`require('./scripts/metro-asset-transformer.cjs')`) and :7 (`transformerPath: require.resolve(...)`) load the guard during config construction. The config process only needs the image-size decoder guard (line 11), but this pulls the whole transform-worker toolchain (@babel/core, metro-minify-terser, metro-transform-plugins, source-map, ...) into every config load: bounded tracing (fd 3 markers from cba1eabf, extended with process.resourceUsage() counters) shows base config-ready at ~633 modules vs ~568 with the fix, and under CPU starvation the require-start:transform-worker -> require-end:babel-core span alone costs ~1.4 s of the 5 s budget (throttle-8pct-base.log: transform-worker starts at 2696 ms, babel-core ends at 4095 ms; the child is SIGKILLed at 5097 ms before config-ready). REPRODUCTION (VERIFIED, through the real Jest harness, not a synthetic probe): /home/ubuntu/throttle-repro.sh (uploaded) runs the focused ICNS test cold (rm -rf $TMPDIR/metro-*, echo 3 > drop_caches) under `systemd-run --scope -p CPUQuota=N%`, base vs candidate wrapper, same quota. CPUQuota=8%: BASE fails with exactly the historical signature — child SIGKILL at 5096.9 ms, config-start emitted, config-ready never reached, last marker inside the transform-worker/babel load (artifacts/p0-01-r3/throttle-8pct-base.log); CANDIDATE at the same quota reaches config-ready at 4695 ms and source-complete at 4698 ms (the whole probe body finishes) but is still killed at 5096.7 ms during process teardown (throttle-8pct-candidate.log) — so 8% is below the floor for either variant on this box, while the fix moves ~1.4 s of work out of the budget. CPUQuota=9% and 10%: base and candidate both pass (throttle-{9,10}pct-*.log). Ordinary cold runs (no throttle) complete config in ~320-360 ms on both. Root-cause classification: MODULE GRAPH — an unnecessary eager toolchain load in the config process (~65 extra modules, ~1.5 MB of reads, ~25 ms CPU unthrottled, ~1.4 s under starvation); not the Metro FileStore cache (the ICNS probe never touches $TMPDIR/metro-cache; fsRead differs by only ~1.5k between variants) and not page-fault/IO bound (majorPageFault 0 in the throttled runs, ~100 in isolated cold-page-cache runs for both variants). INFERRED: the intermittent CI/shared-runner timeout is this same CPU-contention mechanism, since the deadline miss is reproducible only by CPU starvation and the killed phase matches. FIX: lazy `transform`/`getCacheKey` getters in the guard wrapper (decoder guard still eager; interface unchanged; see approach).
